 8:51 pm, November 7, 2026 No. 7 Texas, No. 8 UCLA survive 
 We almost had some unexpected endings within the noon slate, but the usual suspects survived another week.
 No. 8 UCLA outlasted Minnesota, 34-20 and, in similar fashion, No. 7 Texas surged late to top No. 18 Missouri 34-20 in a fourth-quarter scramble.
 Ty Dieffenbach went 8-of-16 but picked up 303 yards through the air and three passing touchdowns.
 Dieffenbach leaned heavily on Aidan Mizell, who recorded 150 receiving yards, and Wayne Knight who grabbed 109 yards on 18 carries. 
 UNBELIEVABLE!! BACK-TO-BACK 75-YARD TDs!! 📺: FOX https://t.co/uPN5YoRYny
— UCLA Football (@UCLAFootball) November 7, 2026 
 With the help of Arch Manning, Texas’ receiving room racked up 297 yards and three touchdowns.
 The Longhorns' defense worked their magic, even without Colin Simmons, limiting the Tigers to 84 yards on the ground.
 SNAGGED IT🤯 https://t.co/LBxsL8oR5P
— Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 7, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 8:33 pm, November 7, 2026 No. 3 Utah stays undefeated, wins 28-20 over No. 9 BYU
 For No. 3 Utah, it may just feel something like 2004.
 The last time the Utes began their season 10-0 was 22 years ago under Urban Meyer. They went on to become the first non-BCS team to play in a BCS bowl game.
 This was three years before the first iPhone was released. Mean Girls was in theaters, NASA landed two rovers on Mars...and Utah was No. 4 in the country. 
 Now, it’s 2026, Utah is one of three undefeated FBS teams left and Morgan Scalley is the first Utah coach to start his career with nine straight wins. Scalley, of course, played for Utah's ‘04 team. 
 After a 28-20 win over No. 9 BYU in the 104th edition of the Holy War, Utah holds the longest active streak in FBS with 15.
 #GoUtes | #RSNB | 📺 ABC https://t.co/v2THpjW11O
— Utah Football (@Utah_Football) November 7, 2026 
 Utes signal caller Devon Dampier went 14-of-26 for 177 passing yards and two touchdowns. Oh, and he also caught a 29-yard pass from wide receiver Creed Whittemore. On the ground, Dampier picked up 87 yards and two more touchdowns.
 The BYU offense ebbed and flowed, but Bear Bachmeier's four interceptions, one of which sealed the game as the clock expired, did the Cougars in.
 share with Facebook copy link 8:19 pm, November 7, 2026 Florida State nabs first road win since 2023
 The drought is over, FSU fans.
 The last time the Seminoles won a road game was in 2023. Now, in their first game after firing Mike Norvell, Florida State has notched a 31-24 win over Boston College at Alumni Stadium.
 A kicker touchdown, a lights out secondary, a gutsy quarterback and an interim head coach might have been just what Florida State needed.
 The first career rushing TD for @Amari_Thomas4 ‼️ #NoleFamily https://t.co/bS4PBQcykp
— FSU Football (@FSUFootball) November 7, 2026 
 As we enter the Rick Stockstill era, we can't forget that this is just another coaching gig on his resumé.
 For Stockstill, a former FSU quarterback, things are full circle. He led the Seminoles to a 10-2 record, a No. 5 AP ranking in 1980 and some of their most important wins in school history early in the Bobby Bowden tenure.
 Stockstill completed 250 passes for 2,834 yards and 26 touchdowns in his career wearing gold and maroon.

 share with Facebook copy link 7:23 pm, November 7, 2026 Duke stuns NC State with a KICK SIX before halftime 🤯
 I mean, that's one way to end the half.
 Duke's Andrew Pellicciotta stood deep in the NC State end zone as Kanoah Vinesett lined up for a 50-yard field goal, hoping to nab three more points for the Wolfpack before heading to the locker room.
 The kick fell short, though, right into the hands of Pillicciotta, who returned the ball 109 yards for a touchdown, extending the Blue Devils' lead to 31-3. 
 WHAT A WAY TO END THE HALF! ANDREW PELLICCIOTTA 109 YARDS!!! https://t.co/ObchjXtY7C
— Duke Football (@DukeFOOTBALL) November 7, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 7:02 pm, November 7, 2026 Interim-led Florida State scores on kicker TD
 What a wild week it's been for Florida State.
 After starting their season 3-5 and coming off a 36-24 home loss to Clemson, the Seminoles fired longtime head coach Mike Norvell, bumping up Rick Stockstill into FSU's interim coaching spot.
 Despite a tough beginning, Stockstill, a former FSU quarterback, has shown that there's still some fight left in this year's Seminole squad.
 Florida State leads Boston College 21-17 in the third quarter and just faked a field goal for a touchdown scored by the kicker.
 Yes, you read that right. Check out this clip.
 Just like we drew it up @GPanikowski #NoleFamily https://t.co/0ub1GaUd77
— FSU Football (@FSUFootball) November 7, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 6:34 pm, November 7, 2026 Touching base on the noon window
 What a way to start the noon slate and what a bad day to be a wedding guest. 
 We could be looking at potential losses for two of the last three undefeated FBS teams, so let’s dive into some scores and stats of today’s early games, all at the half.
 No. 9 BYU 20, No. 3 Utah 14 
 In 104 editions of the Holy War, this is the first time both teams are ranked in the top 10.
 For the opening quarter, it was all Utes. 
 Utah’s offense had racked up over 100 yards with just over five minutes of possession, averaging almost 20 yards per play on their first few drives. 
 Down 14-0, the Cougars didn’t waver, capitalizing off of offensive weapons and fumble recoveries. 
BYU notched 20 points since the Utes' last lead, holding Utah to just 30 yards.
 With Bear Bachmeier at the helm and L.J. Martin back on the field, BYU has rallied back to take the lead.  
 WELCOME BACK LJ MARTIN!!! 📺 ABC https://t.co/6JeyZWtrjP
— BYU FOOTBALL (@BYUfootball) November 7, 2026 
 After the Cougars snatched a loose ball from Utes signal caller Devon Dampier, Bachmeier recorded his fifth interception of the season before giving Utah another shot at the end zone before heading into the locker room, but BYU's defense held up.
 No. 7 Texas 10, No. 18 Missouri 10  
 Well, it’s been quite a long time since Missouri has had two top-10 wins at home — 87 years, to be exact.
 When looking at the box score, the similarities between the two team's offenses are uncanny.
 Both quarterbacks have around 120 yards through the air and a touchdown a piece. Both rushing units have just over 50 yards. Both receiver rooms have over 100 yards. And both teams, each 6-2, have 10 points each.
 But Missouri's defense is what stands out. The Tigers' ability to limit Arch Manning and the Longhorns' rushers has been a part of Missouri's scheme to keep this one close.
 🔥🔥 https://t.co/MT0Ufm6pSm
— Mizzou Football (@MizzouFootball) November 7, 2026 
 No. 8 UCLA 10, Minnesota 10 
 It ain’t over till it’s over. 
 If one thing’s for certain, Minnesota isn’t afraid to poke any bears — or Bruins, so to speak. 
 The Gophers have big wins over Michigan and No. 19 Iowa, and even gave No. 4 Indiana a run for their money last week, forcing the Hoosiers into overtime. 
 Minnesota notched a 38-yard field goal to tie things up before the half, biting at the Bruins' ankles. 
 No. 8 UCLA 10, Minnesota 10 Luke Drzewiecki's FG as time expires in the first half knots things up in Minneapolis. Watch on FOX https://t.co/x0lXcCk22Q
— Big Ten Network (@BigTenNetwork) November 7, 2026 
 share with Facebook copy link 4:29 pm, November 7, 2026 What we're excited about today
 If today doesn't have anything to offer you, nothing will.
 There are SEVEN ranked vs. ranked games today, so Tuesday's second College Football Playoff rankings are going to look rather different.
 No. 3 Utah hosts rival No. 9 BYU for the Holy War
 No. 7 Texas visits No. 18 Missouri 
 Lane Kiffin and No. 14 LSU play rival No. 5 Alabama 
 No. 12 Ohio State has to regroup from a second loss by playing No. 23 Oregon 
 No. 6 Kentucky takes on rival No. 13 Tennessee 
 No. 1 Miami goes into a hostile environment to take on No. 11 Notre Dame at night
 No. 10 Ole Miss has another huge home game this season, hosting No. 2 Georgia after getting a visit from LSU in September
 ESPN's "College GameDay" is in South Bend, where the Irish will face a Miami team without star WR Malachi Toney, who will reportedly need surgery for a high ankle sprain .
 In another other top-10 game, BYU star RB LJ Martin will be back after an ankle injury. Martin hasn't played since Oct. 3. He is averaging 7.8 yards per attempt this season — one year after rushing for 1,305 yards and 12 TDs.
 Over in the SEC, Ole Miss, Tennessee and Missouri and LSU all want to remain firmly in the CFP chase by winning at home and avoiding a third loss, with the Rebels having to do so without RB Kewan Lacy.
 share with Facebook copy link 3:56 pm, November 7, 2026 No. 22 Arizona stuns TCU after recovered pooch
 We've already had some ranked chaos this weekend, as No. 22 Arizona used late drama to beat TCU 29-28 on Friday. 
 The Wildcats improved to 7-2 overall and 4-2 in the Big 12 on a Michael Salgado-Medina 37-yard kick in the final minute after they recovered a pooch kick. That followed a Noah Fifita 15-yard TD pass and failed two-point conversion that made the game 28-26.
 Fifita finished with 313 passing yards and three total touchdowns. TCU QB Jaden Craig accounted for three touchdowns himself but the Wildcats out-gained the Horned Frogs 441-281.
 KICK IS GOOD ‼️ WILDCATS TAKE THE LEAD. https://t.co/tyzKy15aXO
— Arizona Football (@ArizonaFBall) November 7, 2026
